clue.text: Hammer thrower has a number on his chest

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, wields and hurls the hammer Mjolnir
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An athlete in the hammer event wears a competition number pinned to his shirt front.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a track-and-field hammer thrower, but the thrower is a god.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the anatomical term for the upper trunk between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Wing patterns have changed

indicators.note: the letters of the word before have altered their order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the designs in one wing of a building are different now.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, so it is a wing of the building.

clue.text: How bounders are caught unawares?

parts.note: bounders read literally as leaping animals such as kangaroos, which would be caught mid-jump; the idiom means caught off guard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounders' sounds like the old word for cads, but it means creatures that bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught unprepared is the idiomatic sense; mid-leap is the literal joke for anything that jumps.

clue.text: Come up against an objection

parts.note: the indefinite article gives A
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a protest raised at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or touch, meeting something at its edge.

clue.text: Giving a signal when slowing down

definitions.meaning: waving a flag to send a message

explanation.surface: A driver uses hand signals while easing off the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Signalling with flags is one sense; tiring or drooping is the other.

clue.text: Fail to win a single game and get annoyed

parts.note: to lose is not to win
patience is the British name for solitaire, a card game for one player

explanation.surface: A player loses at solitaire and becomes irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: PATIENCE is the British name for solitaire, the one-player card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's temper or growing irritable is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Less than a pint means a breather for some drinkers

definitions.meaning: the breathing organ of fish, which take in water constantly

explanation.surface: Ordering less than a pint lets some drinkers pause between rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinkers' suggests pub-goers; here they are fish, which 'drink' water through their breathing organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is a quarter-pint measure, and also the organ a fish uses for respiration.

clue.text: It can't be made whole

indicators.note: the letters are to be made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken object is beyond repair.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a statement about something unmendable, but 'It can't' is the fodder and 'whole' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means undamaged and complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Decline to leave university

definitions.meaning: British universities say students come down at the end of term or their course

explanation.surface: A student refuses to quit their degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'go up' to university (especially Oxford or Cambridge) and 'go down' when you leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling in value is one sense; departing an Oxbridge college at term's end is the other.

clue.text: King for half a year and one short day

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word year is kept, two of its four letters
the abbreviated weekday loses one letter, its final one

parts.note: Thurs is the short form of Thursday

explanation.surface: A monarch reigned for six months and one brief day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps AR, the back half of YEAR; 'one short' cuts the S from THURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur is the legendary British king of Camelot.

clue.text: Ring in wrong details and get cut off

indicators.note: the ring shape is put inside the rearranged letters
the letters are wrongly ordered, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone phones in incorrect information and the line goes dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DETAILS into ISLATED, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated is separated and alone, remote from others.

clue.text: They may be running the moment race is organised

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The race is laid out and broadcasters are ready to talk through the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Running commentaries are live descriptions of events as they happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters give running descriptions of sporting events as they unfold.

clue.text: Stop-this is a hold up

definitions.meaning: to staunch or check a flow
the stalk that supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A robber shouts that it is a stick-up and everyone must freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to staunch it; a plant's stalk is what supports its bloom.

clue.text: An animal that's shy backs up

parts.note: coy means bashful

indicators.note: the following word is read backwards, as if backing up

explanation.surface: A timid creature retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: A direction to lower a boat

parts.note: S stands for south, a compass point
a cow lows, so read as a mooer it is something that lows

explanation.surface: An instruction to lower a boat into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like 'let down', but read it as 'one that lows', i.e. moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight.

clue.text: Chap on the base gets permit

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: Al is a common man's name
low means base or mean

explanation.surface: A man stationed at a military base receives a pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to let or give leave for something.

clue.text: Moslem leader said to be virtuous

indicators.note: the first letter leads the word

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A Muslim cleric is reported to be a righteous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a title such as imam, but it means the first letter of 'Moslem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral means upright and principled.

clue.text: Announcement from the Roman Capitol

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An edict issued from the Capitol in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' indicates the answer is made from the letters of ROMAN CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclamation is a formal public declaration.

clue.text: A sharp fall in sweet production?

parts.note: acid means sour-tasting
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: Confectionery output suffers a steep decline.
explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a sharp-tasting boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: This tart boiled candy is a confection that factories turn out.

clue.text: Starfish disclosed by tides or a storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A starfish is washed up by the tides or a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroid is the zoological term for a starfish, from the class Asteroidea.

clue.text: Faces sanctions?

explanation.surface: A question whether someone confronts penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanctions' looks like penalties, but here it is the verb meaning approves.
explanation.definitionFit: Visages are the noun sense; to approve or tolerate is the verb sense.

clue.text: Empty one container into another

indicators.note: the first pieces go into the other container

parts.note: a vat is another container
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Someone pours one vessel out into a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied.

clue.text: Misdeed on a battleground Fr

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a crime is a misdeed

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing is committed on a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimea, a peninsula on the Black Sea, was the scene of the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula was the theatre of the Crimean War of 1853-56.

clue.text: Bill received in connection with port

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
re means concerning

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives relating to a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a historic harbour town in northern Israel.

clue.text: Tom honoured in song

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: A man called Tom is praised in a ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, an award in the British honours system.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a round for several voices, often humorous.

clue.text: Move slowly to the border

explanation.surface: Someone creeps toward the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Inching along is the verb sense; a rim or margin is the noun sense.

clue.text: Worn part of a brake

parts.note: the friction pad of a brake gets worn down, and something worn on the foot shares its name

explanation.definitionFit: A brake block pressing on a wheel and footwear share the name.

clue.text: Fight blows up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: raps are blows

explanation.surface: A brawl erupts.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue.

clue.text: Seat of unusual charm and appearance

indicators.note: the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A chair notable for its odd charm and good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CHARM into ARMCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a seat with side supports for the arms.

clue.text: City's side at sea in scoreless draw

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a nil-nil result, written as two zeros
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A city's football team play a goalless match at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Oporto (Porto) is Portugal's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, in English often Oporto, is a major Portuguese city famed for its wine.

clue.text: Go over new art and poetry

indicators.note: the letters are made new, rearranged

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone revisits fresh art and poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or travel over.

clue.text: How one felt, left in the dark

definitions.text: How one felt, left in the dark

parts.words: How one felt, left in the dark
parts.note: the surface suggests emotion at being uninformed; literally, someone in darkness feels about with hands

explanation.definitionFit: To grope is to search blindly by touch.
